items.title: 8.3 Relation between macroscopic and microscopic events

blocks.text: Macroscopic events are the result of multiple simultaneous microscopic events, so understanding the microscopic events helps to explain and predict the observed macroscopic changes in an equilibrium system. When an equilibrium shifts, the microscopic events that explain the observed changes are the collisions and the formation of new bonds between particles; these collisions change the rates of the forward and reverse reactions, which are affected by the activation energy and by external factors, and together they appear as macroscopic changes visible to the naked eye.
